consequence_for_the_split: The re-freeze remains motivated, but on the COVERAGE axis, not the series-depth axis. Carving a population-matched panel should match train scaffold support; matching series depth would if anything make the panel look worse, not better.

declared_before_run.falling: uninformative on its own -- support helping and depth not hurting are indistinguishable
declared_before_run.flat: negative result; series structure is not the mechanism
declared_before_run.rising: conservative evidence for the series-depth mechanism, since support rises with depth and should lower error

finding: Identity NLL FALLS monotonically with analogue-series depth, from 3.87 at depth 1 to 2.42 at depth 25+. The direction is the opposite of the prediction, and it survives both available controls: at fixed zero train support (n=5,863) it falls 3.90->2.39, and within the 0-24 heavy-atom band (n=6,992, mean size flat at 20.0 across buckets) it falls 4.30->2.15. So it is neither the support effect nor a branching-factor artifact. The panel's WORST entries are its 1,786 shallow singleton-scaffold entries at ~3.7-3.9; its 9,959 deep-series entries are its BEST at 2.42. Since the panel is 70% deep-series, congeneric structure is not what depresses panel performance -- it flatters it.

panel_scaffold_coverage_vs_compiled_trai.why_superseded: 0.855 counted train-ROLE sources over 30 Active8 shards; the model trained on the compiled library of 106,759 of 564,316 role sources

prediction_under_test: identity NLL RISES monotonically with panel series depth
reading: Both axes plausibly measure the same latent quantity -- how typical the chemistry is. A deep panel series means a generic scaffold; high train support means a seen scaffold. The worst cell is the unusual one-off: singleton panel scaffold with zero train support. This is associational, not causal: depth was not manipulated.
what_the_gap_does_track: Train scaffold support. Support 25+ scores 1.94 against 2.84 at zero support, and 41.5% of panel entries sit on a scaffold with no training-library source. Support-matching the panel would move identity NLL from 2.62 to about 1.94, roughly 0.69 nats or 26%. Note the effect is not smooth: zero support (2.84) and support 1-4 (2.93) are indistinguishable, so only heavy support helps.
